To evaluate the association between brain activation and hormones, two regression analyses were conducted with E2 or P4 level as a predictor and DLPFC activity as a dependent variable.

Thirty-two adolescent girls were recruited; three girls with contraceptive use and one girl who declined to complete the fMRI session were excluded, leaving 28 peri-pubertal girls in the final sample.

value: Declined to complete the fMRI session

recruitment_method.value: Supplementary study from an ongoing NIMH-funded neuroimaging study at the Olin Neuropsychiatry Research Center

clinical_characteristics.value: No psychiatric diagnoses; approximately 85% were advanced or post-puberty and 14% were mid-puberty. No participants were left-handed.

description.value: Participants viewed positive, negative, and neutral IAPS images and used cognitive reappraisal to decrease, increase, or naturally experience their emotional reactions.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to naturally experience, decrease, or increase their emotional reaction to each image, then rate how negative or positive the image made them feel.

stimuli.value: International Affective Pictures System images: 15 positive, 15 negative, and 5 neutral images per run.
